questions.q: Benzaldehyde is heated with acetic anhydride and sodium acetate, and the mixture is acidified. The main product is:
questions.explain: The anhydride carbanion adds to the aldehyde, and hydrolysis plus dehydration give C₆H₅CH=CHCOOH, mainly the more stable trans (E) isomer, with acetic acid as by-product.

questions.q: Benzaldehyde is heated with propanoic anhydride and sodium propanoate. The product after work-up is:
questions.explain: The α-carbon of propanoic anhydride carries a methyl group, and it becomes doubly bonded to the aldehyde carbon, giving α-methylcinnamic acid. The salt matches the anhydride so no mixed products form.

questions.q: Which anhydride can NOT be used to build the C=C bond in a Perkin reaction with benzaldehyde?
questions.explain: The anhydride needs two α-hydrogens on the same carbon: one is removed to form the carbanion and the second is lost when the C=C forms. The (CH₃)₂CH–CO group has only one α-H.

questions.q: Salicylaldehyde (2-hydroxybenzaldehyde) is heated with acetic anhydride and sodium acetate. The product is:
questions.explain: The cinnamic-acid-type side chain closes onto the neighbouring phenol OH to form a six-membered lactone, coumarin. The open-chain hydroxy acid is only an intermediate, which is the trap.
